drills.q: State the Chinchilla scaling result and the compute-budget arithmetic behind it.
drills.a: N and D both scale as C^0.5 for fixed compute C; optimal ratio ~20 tokens/param. FLOPs ~= 6ND connects budget to N and D.

drills.q: Why did LLaMA train deliberately past the Chinchilla-optimal ratio?
drills.a: A smaller model cheaper to serve at inference beats a training-FLOP-optimal larger model once serving cost (paid indefinitely) is accounted for.

drills.q: Explain MinHash+LSH deduplication mechanically and why it avoids O(n^2) comparison.
drills.a: Documents represented as n-gram shingle sets; MinHash signature approximates Jaccard similarity; signature split into bands, documents matching within any band go into a candidate bucket -- only bucket-mates get directly compared.

drills.q: Why does FineWeb deduplicate per-snapshot instead of globally?
drills.a: Global dedup was found to systematically favor whichever snapshot was processed first/last, discarding valuable older content due to processing order rather than quality.

drills.q: What did Muennighoff et al. find about repeating pretraining data across epochs?
drills.a: Up to ~4 epochs: negligible degradation. Up to ~16 epochs: diminishing but real gains. By ~40 epochs: benefit essentially gone; marginal value of k-th repeat decays geometrically.

drills.q: Derive the compute-time estimate for training a 7B model at Chinchilla ratio on an 8-GPU node.
drills.a: D~1.4e11 tokens, FLOPs=6ND~5.9e21. At ~1.5e15 FLOP/s achievable on 8xA100, time ~3.9e6s ~= 45 days.

drills.q: What is 'curriculum' in modern LLM pretraining and how does it differ from classic curriculum learning?
drills.a: Staged domain mixture (web-heavy then curated/synthetic mid-training stage), not per-example easy-to-hard ordering as in classic curriculum learning.

drills.q: A staged (curriculum) training run underperforms a uniform-mixture baseline at the same token budget. First hypothesis?
drills.a: The LR schedule -- curriculum training needs a more moderate decay than uniform training; reusing the uniform schedule wastes the late high-quality stage's value.

drills.q: What's the difference between heuristic filtering and classifier-based quality filtering in data curation?
drills.a: Heuristic filtering uses fixed rules (length, alphabetic ratio, boilerplate); classifier-based filtering scores documents against a reference-quality target and is reported as the largest per-token quality lever in most pipelines.

drills.q: Design the data pipeline and scaling-law approach for a $2M budget with 500B unique tokens.
drills.a: Dedup+quality-filter first to get the real usable token count; fit IsoFLOP scaling laws on the actual filtered pipeline at small scale; decide model size vs repetition tradeoff using Muennighoff's discount curve; bias smaller/more-overtrained if serving at real production traffic.
